title: Finite open filtration for constructible finite local models
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian (every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes). Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ on every small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $F$ be a constructible $B_X$-module sheaf in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Thus $F$ has a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which the restrictions have finite constant local models: pro-étale locally they are $B_T\otimes_{\underline{\Lambda(*)}}\underline P$ with $P$ a finitely presented $\Lambda(*)$-module. There are a nonnegative integer $r$, a chain of open subschemes
$$\varnothing=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_r=X,$$
and reduced closed subschemes [def-pc-reduced-scheme] $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ with underlying sets $V_k\setminus V_{k-1}$, such that each $L_k=(t_k)^*(F|_{V_k})$ has a finite constant local model. If $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ denotes the open immersion and $F_k=v_{k!}v_k^*F$ denotes its counit image in $F$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-upper-star], then these counits are monomorphisms and
$$0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_r=F,\qquad F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k.$$
The quotient isomorphisms are natural in $F$ for a fixed such stratification; $(t_k)_*$ is ordinary closed direct image [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. All the open immersions $v_k$, and the open complements of the $t_k$, are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. All sites use the fixed small-site universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. No local Noetherianity of the structure sheaf, finite type over a field, or local freeness of $L_k$ is required; integral torsion local models are allowed.

source.place: Tag 09Y5 (lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification), finite good refinement of a finite locally closed partition. The sheaf formulation uses the exact open-closed localization sequence recorded in lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed; it is an additional extraction, with the ordering, reduced strata and extension-by-zero subquotients stated explicitly.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every subset of the underlying space of $X$ is quasi-compact. In particular every open subscheme is quasi-compact. For any such scheme $W$, the inverse image of each affine open under its diagonal is a subset of $|X|$ and hence quasi-compact; this proves quasi-separatedness directly from [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. For an open immersion between these schemes its diagonal has the same property, and inverse images of affine opens are subsets of $|X|$, proving that all the open immersions below are qcqs. Now unpack [sk-def-sfb-constructible] on the resulting qcqs scheme $X$: choose a finite partition by constructible locally closed strata $X_a$ with their immersion maps, on which $F$ has finite constant local models over $B_{X_a}$.

source.place: Part (2), definition of constructible sheaves; qcqs consequence from the Noetherian topology

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-good-stratification-refinement] to the underlying topological space of $X$ and the finite locally closed partition chosen in step 1. Its descending-chain hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $X$. Obtain a finite good partition $|X|=\coprod_bQ_b$ refining the original strata, with each stratum closure a union of members. For $X=\varnothing$, take the empty partition. No scheme structure or sheaf assertion is taken from this topology lemma; reduced strata and local-model restrictions are constructed in steps 3 and 4.

source.place: Tag 09Y5, lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification, statement and proof; good stratification: definition-good-stratification

proof.text: A finite good stratification has the partial order $S_i\le S_j$ when $S_i\subseteq\overline{S_j}$, and $\overline{S_j}=\bigcup_{S_i\le S_j}S_i$. Choose a linear extension with maximal strata first. Let $V_k$ be the union of the first $k$ strata and put $V_0=\varnothing$. The first $k$ strata form an upward-closed set for this order, so the complement is a finite union of strata containing the closure of each of its members; hence the complement is closed and $V_k$ is open. Therefore $S_k=V_k\setminus V_{k-1}$ is closed in $V_k$. Give this closed subset its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $t_k:S_k\hookrightarrow V_k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every $V_k$ and every open complement of $t_k$ is quasi-compact; the diagonal-preimage argument in step 1 also proves quasi-separatedness for these schemes and immersions.

source.place: Tag 09Y5 (lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification) together with Tag 09Y0 (definition-good-stratification) and the remark following it (the order and the closure formula); reduced structure from Schemes Tag 01J3

proof.text: Write the original stratum immersion as $X_a\hookrightarrow W_a\hookrightarrow X$, closed followed by open. Since $S_k$ is reduced and its image is contained in $|X_a|$, its map to $X$ factors first through $W_a$ and then through the closed subscheme $X_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme]. Denote the resulting map by $g:S_k\to X_a$. By [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp], $L_k$ identifies with $g^*(F|_{X_a})$. For a trivializing cover $U_i\to X_a$ in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], base change gives a pro-étale cover $U_i\times_{X_a}S_k\to S_k$ by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](1). On this cover a scalar presentation $B_{U_i}^{m}\xrightarrow{A_i}B_{U_i}^{n}\to F|_{U_i}\to0$ pulls back to the same finite matrix $A_i$ with entries in $\Lambda(*)$. Indeed inverse image preserves cokernels and tensor products by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](3)--(4) and [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal], and [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] identifies the inverse image coefficient with the coefficient on the base change. The cokernel is therefore $B_{U_i\times_{X_a}S_k}\otimes_{\underline{\Lambda(*)}}\underline P_i$ for the same finitely presented scalar module $P_i$. This proves the finite constant local-model condition for $L_k$, including torsion modules.

source.place: Part (1)--(2), pullback of the finite constant local-model condition

proof.text: For each $k$, let $Z_k\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closed complement $X\setminus V_k$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to the complementary quasi-compact open immersion $v_k:V_k\hookrightarrow X$ and this closed immersion, with coefficient ring $B_X$. Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] to identify internal modules with sectionwise module sheaves over $B_X$; the equivalence preserves underlying abelian sheaves and their linear maps. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] the inverse-image module functor in that sequence is the module pullback $v_k^*$, and [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] identifies its extension by zero with $v_{k!}$: both lift the abelian extension by zero with the action induced by pulling back $B_X$; equivalently, [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] gives the same left adjoint to the lifted restriction functor, so the unique adjunction comparison identifies their counits. The sequence gives $0\to v_{k!}v_k^*F\to F$, so the counit defining $F_k$ is monic. For $k=r$, $V_r=X$ and this map is an isomorphism, while $V_0=\varnothing$ gives $F_0=0$.

source.place: literature/stacks-project/proetale.tex Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open) and 09BN (lemma-open-immersion), open--closed exact sequence; literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero) and 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact) for extension by zero of modules

proof.text:
Let $a:V_{k-1}\hookrightarrow V_k$. The immersions $a$ and $t_k$ are complementary. By the module comparisons of step 5, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] applied to $F|_{V_k}$ gives the natural short exact sequence
$$0\to a_!a^*(F|_{V_k})\to F|_{V_k}\to(t_k)_*L_k\to0.$$
The functor $v_{k!}$ is exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. To compare its first term with $F_{k-1}$, [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] and [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] give the adjunctions $a_!\dashv a^*$ and $v_{k!}\dashv v_k^*$. Consequently for every module $M$ on $V_{k-1}$ and $N$ on $X$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(v_{k!}a_!M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{V_{k-1}}(M,a^*v_k^*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{V_{k-1}}(M,v_{k-1}^*N),$$
where the last comparison is [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. This identifies $v_{k!}a_!$ with $v_{k-1!}$ as left adjoints. For $M=v_{k-1}^*F$, the composite of the two counits corresponds to the identity of $v_{k-1}^*F$, hence equals the counit into $F$ under this identification. Applying $v_{k!}$ to the short exact sequence therefore gives
$$0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k\to0,$$
with the first map compatible with the embeddings into $F$. This proves the inclusions and quotient isomorphism. The closed direct image is the ordinary module pushforward of [def-sfb-module-lower-star].

proof.text: All maps in the two localization sequences are counits, units, restrictions, or the canonical extension-by-zero comparison just described. Each is natural under a morphism of $F$ while the chosen good stratification is held fixed. The diagram of short exact sequences therefore induces natural quotient isomorphisms $F_k/F_{k-1}\cong v_{k!}(t_k)_*L_k$.
